## NASA-9 polynomial data (`use-nasa9-cp`, `data/nasa9.dat`) {#sec-ch02-nasa9}

### Summary

A constant heat capacity is accurate only over a narrow temperature range. kintera ships a table of NASA-9
polynomial coefficients for 293 species, which give heat capacity, enthalpy and entropy as functions of temperature
in two ranges. The table is looked up by species name when the registry is filled. The coefficients are used in three
places: the temperature-dependent heat capacity of @sec-ch03-species-functions when `use-nasa9-cp` is on; the
dimensionless Gibbs energy of the multiphase equilibrium solver (@sec-ch05); and the equilibrium constant of every
reversible reaction in the kinetics (@sec-ch06), whenever any species of the kinetics options has NASA-9 data, whatever
`use-nasa9-cp` says. NASA-9 is the only temperature-dependent heat-capacity form kintera reads; other forms, such as the
Shomate polynomials, are neither read nor converted at the pin, so their coefficients must be converted to NASA-9 or to
a constant `cv_R` by the user.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** $c_p/\mathcal R$, $h/(\mathcal R T)$, $s/\mathcal R$ from nine coefficients per range,
@eq-ch02-nasa9-forms.

**Data.** `data/nasa9.dat` (293 species, 200-1000 K and 1000-6000 K); nine coefficients per range per species.

**Placement.** Looked up by name in the registry reader; evaluated by the thermodynamics and by reverse kinetics.

**Activation.** $c_p$, $c_v$, $u$ only with `use-nasa9-cp: true` (default off); reverse kinetics whenever any species has data.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact polynomial evaluation; no clamp outside 200-6000 K.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$, the kinetics reference pressure [Pa]; $\Delta n_j$, the net change of moles in
reaction $j$ [-]; $a_k$, $k = 0, \dots, 6$, polynomial coefficients, $a_k$ multiplying $T^{k-2}$ in $c_p/\mathcal R$ and so
carrying K$^{2-k}$; $b_1$, $b_2$, integration constants
of enthalpy [K] and entropy [-]; $T_{\mathrm{mid}}$, the range boundary [K].

### Derivation

Within one temperature range the NASA-9 forms are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{c_p}{\mathcal R} &= a_0 T^{-2} + a_1 T^{-1} + a_2 + a_3 T + a_4 T^2 + a_5 T^3 + a_6 T^4 , \\
\frac{h}{\mathcal R T} &= -a_0 T^{-2} + a_1 \frac{\ln T}{T} + a_2 + \frac{a_3 T}{2} + \frac{a_4 T^2}{3}
+ \frac{a_5 T^3}{4} + \frac{a_6 T^4}{5} + \frac{b_1}{T} , \\
\frac{s}{\mathcal R} &= -\frac{a_0 T^{-2}}{2} - a_1 T^{-1} + a_2 \ln T + a_3 T + \frac{a_4 T^2}{2}
+ \frac{a_5 T^3}{3} + \frac{a_6 T^4}{4} + b_2 .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-nasa9-forms}

The second line is $\int c_p\, \mathrm d T$ divided by $\mathcal R T$, with $b_1$ the constant of integration; the
third is $\int c_p\, \mathrm d T / T$ divided by $\mathcal R$, with $b_2$ its constant. Term by term:
$\int a_0 T^{-2}\,\mathrm d T = -a_0 T^{-1}$ and $\int a_0 T^{-3}\,\mathrm d T = -a_0 T^{-2}/2$;
$\int a_1 T^{-1}\,\mathrm d T = a_1 \ln T$ and $\int a_1 T^{-2}\,\mathrm d T = -a_1 T^{-1}$; the powers
$T^k$, $k \ge 0$, integrate to $T^{k+1}/(k+1)$ and $T^k/k$. The Gibbs energy is $g/(\mathcal R T) = h/(\mathcal R T)
- s/\mathcal R$, computed in `nasa9_gibbs_RT` ({{< code src/thermo/nasa9.hpp nasa9_gibbs_RT >}}).

The file stores ten numbers per range, $a_0$ to $a_6$, an unused zero, $b_1$ and $b_2$, as four lines of five
after the species name. `get_nasa9_db` ({{< code src/species.cpp get_nasa9_db >}}) keeps nine of them, dropping the
zero, so index 7 holds $b_1$ and index 8 holds $b_2$.

**Reverse kinetics.** For a reversible reaction $j$, `forward_with_rate_constants`
({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::forward_with_rate_constants >}}) forms the equilibrium constant in
concentration units from the Gibbs energies of @eq-ch02-nasa9-forms:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta_j \frac{g}{\mathcal R T} &= \sum_n \nu_{nj} \frac{g_n}{\mathcal R T} , \\
K_{c,j} &= \exp\!\left(-\Delta_j \frac{g}{\mathcal R T}
+ \Delta n_j \ln \frac{p_{\mathrm{ref}}}{\mathcal R T}\right) ,
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch02-nasa9-kc}

with $\nu_{nj}$ the net stoichiometric coefficient, $\Delta n_j = \sum_n \nu_{nj}$, and $p_{\mathrm{ref}}$ the
kinetics reference pressure (`Pref`[^rg-7058b44e3174], default 101325 Pa). The reverse rate constant is $k_{f,j} / K_{c,j}$, with
$K_{c,j}$ clamped below at $10^{-250}$. The branch runs when the options' `has_nasa9` is true, that is when any
species has a non-zero coefficient; `use-nasa9-cp` is not consulted (verified by reading at the pin).

### Numerical method

The low range is used for $T < T_{\mathrm{mid}}$ and the high range otherwise, chosen per cell and species by a mask.
The registry sets $T_{\mathrm{mid}} = 1000$ K for every species. A species absent from the table gets all-zero
coefficients, and the thermodynamic functions treat a row of zeros as "no NASA-9 data". The table is parsed once per
process, at first use, under a once-flag; `find_resource` locates `nasa9.dat` (a file in the current directory takes
precedence, see the Tests layer).

The NASA-9 figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of the NASA-9 data. {#tbl-ch02-nasa9-code}

Setup checks a user can hit: a missing `nasa9.dat` stops the load; `nasa9_gibbs_rt` refuses a name not in the table
("NASA-9 species not found") and a non-floating-point temperature. `data/nasa9.dat` and `python/data/nasa9.dat` are
identical at the pin (`cmp` of the two files).

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_species.release` (`SpeciesInit.prefers_current_directory_nasa9_file`) | a `nasa9.dat` in the working directory is read, with the coefficient layout above | exact | equality |
| `test_nasa9_cp.py` | with `use-nasa9-cp`, $c_p$ and $c_v$ follow @eq-ch02-nasa9-forms | $10^{-10}$ rel. | not yet derived |
| `test_equilibrium.release` (`Nasa9.ConcurrentFirstDatabaseAccess`) | eight threads reading the table first at once get the same finite $g/(\mathcal R T)$ at 1500 K | `allclose` defaults | PyTorch defaults |

: Tests of the NASA-9 data. {#tbl-ch02-nasa9-tests}

The tolerances are read from the test files at the pin. No test checks the entropy line of @eq-ch02-nasa9-forms or the value of `nasa9_gibbs_RT` against reference data; the
concurrency test checks only finiteness and agreement between threads. That is missing evidence.

### Limits

The polynomials are evaluated outside 200-6000 K without warning (verified by reading `nasa9_gibbs_RT`; no clamp).
$T_{\mathrm{mid}}$ is fixed at 1000 K, which matches the file header's ranges. A working-directory `nasa9.dat`
silently replaces the shipped one.

In reverse kinetics, a species absent from the table has all-zero coefficients, so @eq-ch02-nasa9-forms gives it
$g/(\mathcal R T) = 0$ at every temperature, and it enters $K_{c,j}$ of @eq-ch02-nasa9-kc as if its Gibbs energy were
zero; no warning is printed (verified by reading `get_nasa9_db`, `init_species_from_yaml` and
`forward_with_rate_constants`). If no species of the kinetics options is in the table, the reverse branch does not run:
the reverse rates are not appended, while `reset` ({{< code src/kinetics/kinetics.cpp KineticsImpl::reset >}}) has
already appended a reverse column to the stoichiometry matrix for every reversible reaction. The rate vector is then
shorter than the stoichiometry matrix has columns; what a caller that multiplies the two gets (a shape error or a
silently truncated product) is a hypothesis, not run. No test covers either case: missing evidence.
